I've been working these fields since I was twenty years old. Forty-five years teaches you things no book can. My land is 18.8 mu — I know every corner of it. I farm alone now, so I have to be realistic about what I can manage.

My wheat-maize fields I'll keep at 12 mu. That rotation is solid — winter wheat goes in October, I harvest in June, then I get maize in right away on the same ground, harvest in late September. I've done this my whole life. The remaining 6.8 mu I'll put in cotton. Cotton prices are decent, I know how to grow it, and I've got the well for irrigation.

For wheat, I'll use the improved winter variety from the county seed station — not the fanciest hybrid, just the reliable one I've used for years. Three irrigations: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. That's what the land needs. Rotary till before seeding — saves my back compared to deep ploughing and the soil is fine enough after years of this rotation. Nitrogen I'll split: base and topdressing at jointing. Herbicide in early spring and a fungicide pass if the weather turns wet.

For the summer maize, I go hybrid — everyone in the village does, Zhengdan or something similar. I direct-seed right after wheat harvest, no tillage needed, the ground is already worked. Two irrigations if summer rain is poor, which it often is. Urea topdressing at knee-high and again at tasseling.

Cotton is the heavy work. Spring plough, plant in late April, then it's irrigating, topping, and fighting bugs all summer. Aphids, bollworm — I spray eight times some years. It's hard at my age but I know the crop and I need the income from it.
